Parses and represents an HTTP path template with segments, optional custom verb, and variable bindings. Provides accessors and constants for wildcard keys. Inner struct Variable describes a bound range and field path.

Alias for HTTP method key type used in the trie (e.g., "GET", "POST" possibly with custom verb suffix).

functions.name: google::http::pattern_matcher::PathMatcher<Method>::Lookup
functions.signature: template <class Method> template <class VariableBinding> Method google::http::pattern_matcher::PathMatcher<Method>::Lookup(const std::string& http_method, const std::string& path, const std::string& query_params, std::vector<VariableBinding>* variable_bindings, std::string* body_field_path) const
functions.description: Looks up the Method associated with an HTTP method and URL path, optionally parsing variable bindings from the path and query parameters. Splits the path, performs a trie lookup, and if found, fills variable_bindings with path and non-system query parameter bindings and returns the stored Method. body_field_path is set to the configured body mapping if provided. Returns a null/empty Method when not found or when the route is ambiguous.
requirements: http_method should be the HTTP method string used during registration (case and custom verb concatenation must match registration logic).
path should be a valid request path; it will be sanitized and split internally (query string is ignored here).
query_params should be the raw query string portion without the leading '?'; may be empty.
variable_bindings may be nullptr; if non-null must point to a valid vector and will be cleared/populated by the function.
body_field_path may be nullptr; if non-null must point to a valid std::string to receive the body field path.
The underlying matcher must have been built/initialized; if no routes exist, the function returns a null/empty Method.
If multiple matches are registered for the same route, the function returns a null/empty Method.

functions.name: google::http::pattern_matcher::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::PathMatcherBuilder
functions.description: Default-constructs a PathMatcherBuilder with an empty trie root and default unescape behavior. Used to register routes before building an immutable PathMatcher.

functions.name: google::http::pattern_matcher::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Register
functions.signature: template <class Method> bool google::http::pattern_matcher::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Register(const std::string& http_method, const std::string& http_template, const std::string& body_field_path, const std::unordered_set<std::string>& system_query_parameter_names, Method method)
functions.description: Registers a route mapping (http_method + http_template) to a Method along with a body field path and the set of system query parameter names to ignore during binding extraction. If the template parses and inserts successfully, stores the route in the trie. Replaces any existing mapping for the same template; only the last registered method is kept. Returns false if the http_template is invalid.
requirements: http_template must be a valid HTTP template string parseable by HttpTemplate::Parse; otherwise the function returns false and does not register.
http_method is used as-is and combined with any template verb for registration; it must match the string later used for lookup.
method must be a valid value to store; its lifetime must be suitable for copying/storing inside the builder (it is copied/moved into internal storage).
system_query_parameter_names contains names that will be ignored when extracting query parameter bindings at lookup time.
body_field_path may be empty to indicate no body mapping.
Repeated registrations for the same path/method mark duplicates; only the last one is stored for lookup while duplicates are tracked for ambiguity handling.

Not thread-safe; ensure exclusive access when calling Build().

functions.name: google::http::pattern_matcher::GetEscapedChar

functions.description: Helper for URL unescaping. Checks whether the next three characters at src[i] form a percent-encoded sequence "%XX" and, if so, returns true and writes the decoded byte to out according to the provided unescape policy.

i indexes into src; passing i >= src.size() will result in no match (function returns false).
out must point to valid writable memory if the caller expects the decoded character; if out is nullptr, the decoded value cannot be returned.
unescape_spec controls whether certain escapes should be treated as reserved and possibly not unescaped (see UrlUnescapeSpec).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets PathMatcherBuilder::Register fuzz stub.
# The stub constructs:
#  - http_method chosen internally between "GET" or "POST" (from FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)).
#  - Two FUZZ_PARAM_STR() used as path segments seg1 and seg2, sanitized:
#       * truncated to 32
#       * '/' replaced with '_'
#       * if s is "." or ".." -> "seg"
#       * if empty -> "seg"
#    Then http_template = "/" + seg1 + "/" + seg2
#  - body_field_path chosen internally between "" and "msg.body"
#
# Our task: produce an input buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR will read from to get
# interesting, yet valid segment strings. We cannot control FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int),
# but we can provide multiple candidate strings so that different executions exercise
# various cases. We'll encode a simple length-prefixed sequence of UTF-8 strings
# that common fuzz harnesses (including LLVMFuzzer custom providers) can consume.
#
# Format we emit:
#   [count:1 byte]
#   repeated count times:
#       [len:1 byte][bytes:len]
# The total output is <= 4096 bytes. The strings include cases to explore:
#  - simple literals: "users", "items"
#  - reserved-ish but sanitized path chars (no '/')
#  - dot names that would be mapped to "seg" after sanitization: ".", ".."
#  - empty string -> "seg"
#  - maximum length (32 after truncation), with mixed chars
#  - names with slashes which will be replaced by '_' (we include but harness will sanitize)
#  - names containing URL-encoded sequences (kept as-is for template registration)
#  - names with ASCII, digits, hyphen, underscore
#  - random alphanum to diversify trie
#
# The harness likely reads sequentially; we just provide a pool.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def _make_fixed_cases(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cases = [
        "users",
        "items",
        ".",
        "..",
        "",  # becomes "seg"
        "v1",
        "a" * 40,  # will be truncated to 32
        "with/slash",  # '/' -> '_'
        "name-with-dash",
        "name_with_underscore",
        "percent%20space",
        "hex%2Fslash",  # contains %2F but slash literal not present; stays as text
        "col:on",       # colon allowed, tests verb handling downstream (though builder only registers path)
        "123",
    ]
    # add a couple of random 32-char mixes (no '/') to ensure variety
    for _ in range(3):
        s = ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM + "-_.") for _ in range(32))
        cases.append(s)
    # Add variants that would be empty after filtering? Not applicable, but add spaces removed by sanitization? Not removed; keep.
    return cases


def _encode_strings(strs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # length-prefixed 1-byte each; clip to 255 when encoding
    out = bytearray()
    count = min(len(strs), 255)
    out.append(count)
    for s in strs[:count]:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 255:
            b = b[:255]
        out.append(len(b))
        out.extend(b)
        if len(out) >= 4096:
            break
    # ensure <= 4096
    return bytes(out[:4096])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    strs: List[str] = _make_fixed_cases(rnd)

    # Add additional randomized segments to diversify runs
    extra_count = rnd.randint(4, 12)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        choice = rnd.randint(0, 6)
        if choice == 0:
            # random alnum up to 40 (truncated later to 32)
            length = rnd.randint(1, 40)
            s = ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(length))
        elif choice == 1:
            # include slashes (will be replaced by '_')
            parts = [''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 6))) for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4))]
            s = '/'.join(parts)
        elif choice == 2:
            # dot variants
            s = '.' * rnd.randint(1, 3)
        elif choice == 3:
            # kebab/underscore
            base = ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 12)))
            sep = rnd.choice(['-', '_', '.'])
            s = base + sep + ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 12)))
        elif choice == 4:
            # percent-encodings
            tokens = [
                '%20', '%2F', '%3A', '%2b', '%7E', '%25'
            ]
            s = ''.join(rnd.choice(tokens + [rnd.choice(ALNUM)]) for _ in range(rnd.randint(4, 16)))
        elif choice == 5:
            # include colon to potentially form verb-like suffix later in full path
            s = ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 8))) + ':' + ''.join(rnd.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)))
        else:
            # empty (sanitized to "seg") or short
            s = '' if rnd.random() < 0.5 else rnd.choice(['a', 'b', 'c'])
        strs.append(s)

    return _encode_strings(strs)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator crafts valid HTTP path template strings for the library's HttpTemplate::Parse,
# and also valid concrete path strings used by PathMatcherBuilder::Register stub shaping.
# It targets two fuzz stubs:
# 1) PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Register: expects two sanitized segments; we provide inputs
#    that, after the stub's sanitize_segment, form a reasonable template like "/seg1/seg2".
# 2) TransformHttpTemplate: expects a valid HTTP template; we produce patterns such as
#    "/lit/lit", "/lit/{var}", "/{var}/lit", "/{var=*}", "/{var=**}", wildcards, and optional verbs.
# The fuzzer framework will supply FUZZ_PARAM_STR() from our bytes buffer; we concatenate multiple
# candidate strings separated by newlines so the harness can slice them as needed.

SAFE_SEG_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_~."
VAR_NAME_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_seg(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, SAFE_SEG_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_var_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=8) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, VAR_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _make_literal_template(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return f"/{_rand_seg(rng)}/{_rand_seg(rng)}"


def _make_single_var_template(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., "/x/{y}" or "/{id}/users"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"/{_rand_seg(rng)}/{{{_rand_var_name(rng)}}}"
    else:
        return f"/{{{_rand_var_name(rng)}}}/{_rand_seg(rng)}"


def _make_var_with_wildcard(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., "/files/{path=*}" or "/files/{path=**}"
    star = "**" if rng.random() < 0.4 else "*"
    return f"/{_rand_seg(rng)}/{{{_rand_var_name(rng)}={star}}}"


def _make_multi_segment_template(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of literals and single-parameter variables
    parts: List[str] = []
    count = rng.randint(2, 5)
    for i in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.35:
            parts.append(f"{{{_rand_var_name(rng)}}}")
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_seg(rng))
    return "/" + "/".join(parts)


def _maybe_custom_verb(rng: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    # Append a colon verb occasionally, e.g., ":custom"
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        verb = _rand_seg(rng, 2, 6).lower()
        # keep verb alphabetic to be realistic
        verb = ''.join(ch for ch in verb if ch.isalpha()) or "do"
        return f"{path}:{verb}"
    return path


def _percent_encoded(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Insert some percent-encodings safely in literal segments only
    def enc_char(c: str) -> str:
        return f"%{ord(c):02X}"
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch in SAFE_SEG_CHARS and rng.random() < 0.15:
            out.append(enc_char(ch))
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)


def _make_encoded_literal_template(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    a = _percent_encoded(rng, _rand_seg(rng))
    b = _percent_encoded(rng, _rand_seg(rng))
    return f"/{a}/{b}"


def _shaped_for_register_stub(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # The stub sanitizes each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() into a segment by:
    # - truncating to 32 chars
    # - replacing '/' with '_'
    # - mapping "." or ".." to "seg"
    # - replacing empty with "seg"
    # We provide strings that survive this to interesting distinct values.
    candidates = [
        _rand_seg(rng),
        _rand_seg(rng),
        "users",
        "posts",
        "id",
        "segment_with_dash",
        "v1",
    ]
    rng.shuffle(candidates)
    # Join two segments into a plausible template that TransformHttpTemplate might also parse
    s1 = candidates[0]
    s2 = candidates[1] if len(candidates) > 1 else "seg"
    return f"/{s1}/{s2}"


def _make_templates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    ts: List[str] = []
    ts.append(_make_literal_template(rng))
    ts.append(_make_single_var_template(rng))
    ts.append(_make_var_with_wildcard(rng))
    ts.append(_make_multi_segment_template(rng))
    ts.append(_make_encoded_literal_template(rng))
    ts.append(_shaped_for_register_stub(rng))
    # Add a couple more randomized variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.33:
            t = _make_single_var_template(rng)
        elif choice < 0.66:
            t = _make_multi_segment_template(rng)
        else:
            t = _make_literal_template(rng)
        ts.append(t)
    # Optionally append custom verbs to some
    ts = [_maybe_custom_verb(rng, t) if rng.random() < 0.5 else t for t in ts]
    return ts


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    templates = _make_templates(rng)

    # Ensure inclusion of a known-valid template used in the stub bias
    templates.insert(0, "/x/{y}")

    # Join with newlines; FUZZ framework can consume sequential FUZZ_PARAM_STRs from this buffer
    blob = "\n".join(templates)

    # Ensure size limit
    data = blob.encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzz stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to build
# two path segments used in an HTTP template "/seg1/seg2" and occasionally
# a body_field_path like "msg.body". The stub sanitizes each segment by:
# - truncating to 32 chars
# - replacing '/'
# - disallowing '.', '..', and empty -> becomes 'seg'.
# Therefore, to exercise different code paths in the target (template parsing,
# segment handling, variables, literals), we produce strings that, after the
# stub's sanitize, yield interesting and varied, but valid values. We also
# include cases that become exactly '.', '..', empty, and long strings with
# slashes, to trigger the sanitize branches. We intermix identifier-like
# names, numeric segments, URL-escaped content, and mixed case.
#
# The fuzzer obtains multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values from the same input
# buffer. We will encode our values as a simple length-prefixed string list
# so the harness can deterministically split them. A common format for such
# fuzzers is a sequence of: [count][len][bytes]... We implement a compact,
# self-describing binary format:
#   - 1 byte: count N (number of strings)
#   - For i in 1..N:
#       - 2 bytes big-endian length L
#       - L bytes data
# This is generic and easy to consume by typical fuzz harnesses.
# We ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # ensure doesn't become empty or '.'/'..' accidentally
    if s in (".", "..", ""):  # unlikely, but guard
        s += "_x"
    return s


def _rand_escaped(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    # Include percent-encodings and reserved characters to exercise unescape policies
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~!$&'()*+,;=:@"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.20:
            # percent-encoded byte
            byte = rng.randint(0, 255)
            out.append("%" + format(byte, "02X"))
        elif choice < 0.30:
            out.append('/')  # will be sanitized to '_'
        else:
            out.append(rng.choice(pool))
    s = ''.join(out)
    return s


def _long_with_slashes(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [_rand_ident(rng, 1, 8) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))]
    s = '/'.join(parts)
    # possibly exceed 32 to trigger truncation
    while len(s) < 40:
        s += '/' + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
    return s


def _field_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # dotted field path like msg.body, a.b.c, with optional digits/underscores
    depth = rng.randint(1, 5)
    parts = []
    for i in range(depth):
        start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
        rest_len = rng.randint(0, 8)
        rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rest_len))
        parts.append(start + rest)
    return '.'.join(parts)


def _special_cases() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",           # becomes 'seg'
        ".",          # becomes 'seg'
        "..",         # becomes 'seg'
        "/",          # becomes '_'
        "%2F",        # encoded slash remains percent or decoded by policy
        "%2f",
        "%3Averb",    # colon potentially relevant for custom verbs
        "a:b",        # colon inside seg
        "GET",        # method-like
        "POST",
        "msg",        # for body path combos
        "body",
        "__",
        "0",
        "-",          # literal segment
    ]


def _build_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool = []
    pool.extend(_special_cases())
    # Add random idents and escaped variants
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(_rand_ident(rng))
    for _ in range(6):
        pool.append(_rand_escaped(rng))
    # Include long with slashes to test replacement and truncation
    pool.append(_long_with_slashes(rng))
    # Include a few dotted field path-like strings (though used as segments, sanitize will keep dots)
    for _ in range(3):
        pool.append(_field_path(rng))
    # Ensure diversity and limit length per element <= 64 to avoid huge buffer (sanitize will cut to 32 anyway)
    pool = [s[:64] for s in pool]
    return pool


def _serialize(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Format: 1 byte count, then per string: 2-byte big-endian length, data
    # Cap total to MAX_TOTAL
    b = bytearray()
    count = min(len(strings), 50)  # hard cap
    b.append(count & 0xFF)
    total = 1
    used = 0
    for i in range(count):
        s = strings[i].encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(s) > 1024:
            s = s[:1024]
        # Check if adding this would exceed MAX_TOTAL
        needed = 2 + len(s)
        if total + needed > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        b.extend(len(s).to_bytes(2, 'big'))
        b.extend(s)
        total += needed
        used += 1
    # Fix the count to actual used
    b[0] = used & 0xFF
    return bytes(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _build_string_pool(rng)

    # Select a sequence of strings to feed the FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # The stub currently calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice, but future stubs may call more.
    # We'll output a variety where the first two are tailored to exercise distinct paths.

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Choose seg1 candidates: literal, escaped, special
    seg1_opts = [
        rng.choice(pool),
        _rand_ident(rng, 1, 12),
        _rand_escaped(rng, 3, 18),
        "." if rng.random() < 0.3 else "..",  # will become 'seg'
        _long_with_slashes(rng),               # triggers slash replacement and truncation
    ]
    strings.append(rng.choice(seg1_opts))

    # Choose seg2 candidates: numeric, dotted, reserved-heavy
    seg2_opts = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6))),
        _field_path(rng),
        _rand_escaped(rng, 2, 24),
        "",  # becomes 'seg'
        "%2Fslash%2Finside",
    ]
    strings.append(rng.choice(seg2_opts))

    # Add extra strings to populate the pool for any additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    extras = rng.sample(pool, k=min(len(pool), 10))
    strings.extend(extras)

    return _serialize(strings)

import random
import string
from typing import List

HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"
RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
UNRESERVED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
SLASH = "/"

def _pct(byte_val: int) -> str:
    return "%" + HEX[(byte_val >> 4) & 0xF] + HEX[byte_val & 0xF]

def _rand_byte(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    return rng.randrange(0, 256)

def _make_valid_escape_sequences(rng: random.Random, count: int, include_reserved: bool, include_slash: bool) -> List[str]:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if include_slash and choice < 0.2:
            parts.append(_pct(ord('/')))  # %2F
        elif include_reserved and choice < 0.5:
            parts.append(_pct(ord(rng.choice(RESERVED))))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            parts.append(_pct(ord(rng.choice(UNRESERVED))))
        else:
            parts.append(_pct(_rand_byte(rng)))
    return parts

def _segments_with_variety(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    segs = []
    # Plain segment
    segs.append(''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))))
    # Mixed percent-encodings including reserved and slash
    encs = _make_valid_escape_sequences(rng, rng.randint(1, 4), include_reserved=True, include_slash=True)
    segs.append(''.join(encs))
    # Mixed text with encodings
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED + " ") for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
    insert = _pct(ord(rng.choice("OAZ09")))
    segs.append(base + insert + base[::-1])
    # Edge cases: consecutive percents and boundary-like endings
    segs.append(_pct(0) + _pct(255))
    return segs

def _maybe_append_incomplete_or_lower_hex(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally add lower-case hex and incomplete percent to test negative paths
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        b = rng.randrange(256)
        s += "%" + format(b, "02x")  # lower-case
    elif choice < 0.35:
        s += "%"  # lone percent at end
    elif choice < 0.45:
        s += "%A"  # two chars but second missing
    return s

def _build_query_with_encodings(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a query string-like tail to provide more escapes for UrlUnescapeString
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        key = ''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
        vals = _make_valid_escape_sequences(rng, rng.randint(1, 3), include_reserved=True, include_slash=True)
        val_plain = ''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)))
        val = rng.choice([''.join(vals), val_plain, ''.join(vals) + val_plain])
        pairs.append(f"{key}={val}")
    return '&'.join(pairs)

def _build_urlish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a path-like string that the stubs will pass to unescape helpers
    segs = _segments_with_variety(rng)
    # Interleave reserved characters to exercise unescape policies
    decorated = []
    for s in segs:
        prefix = ''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
        mid = rng.choice([":", ";", ",", "@", "", "-"])
        decorated.append(prefix + s + mid)
    path = "/" + "/".join(decorated)
    # Maybe add custom verb suffix and query-like strings
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        path += ":custom"
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        q = _build_query_with_encodings(rng)
        path += ("?" if rng.random() < 0.9 else "&") + q
    # Occasionally ensure a valid escape near the end for GetEscapedChar i near size
    path = _maybe_append_incomplete_or_lower_hex(rng, path)
    return path

def _mix_cases(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    chars = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.3:
            chars.append(ch.swapcase())
        else:
            chars.append(ch)
    return ''.join(chars)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose between producing a compact string (good for GetEscapedChar index ranges)
    # and a longer URL-like string with many percent-encodings.
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts = []
        # Ensure at least one valid escape
        parts.append(_pct(ord(rng.choice(UNRESERVED + RESERVED + SLASH))))
        # Add additional escapes with variety
        parts.extend(_make_valid_escape_sequences(rng, rng.randint(1, 6), include_reserved=True, include_slash=True))
        # Intermix plain characters
        plain = ''.join(rng.choice(UNRESERVED + RESERVED + " ") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
        s = ''.join(parts) + plain
        s = _maybe_append_incomplete_or_lower_hex(rng, s)
    else:
        s = _build_urlish(rng)
    # Randomly change case of hex digits and letters
    s = _mix_cases(rng, s)
    # Bound size to 4096
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
    return s.encode('utf-8')

import random
import struct
import string

# This generator targets fuzzers that expect "literal path segment" strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and sometimes unsigned ints via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int). The stubs sanitize segments by:
# - truncating length (16 or 32)
# - replacing '/' with '_'
# - disallowing '.', '..', and empty -> replaced with a safe default
# Therefore, we supply already-valid, interesting segments to exercise code paths, plus a small
# supply of unsigned integers for branch choices. The buffer packs multiple NUL-terminated strings
# followed by several 32-bit unsigned integers. FUZZ framework will read sequentially.

MAX_BUF = 4096

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_~."

def rnd_safe_seg(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    # Generate a valid literal path segment (no '/', not '.' or '..').
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS.replace('/', '')) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid exactly '.' or '..'
    if s == '.' or s == '..' or s == '':
        s = 'seg'
    return s

def themed_segments(rng: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    # Provide a variety of interesting literal segments used across stubs
    base = [
        'a', 'b', 'x', 'y', 'name', 'seg', 's', 'alpha', 'beta', 'delta',
        'v1', 'users', 'items', 'resource', 'data', 'get', 'post', 'PUT',
    ]
    # Add random safe segments of variable sizes (1..32)
    base += [rnd_safe_seg(rng, 1, 8), rnd_safe_seg(rng, 1, 12), rnd_safe_seg(rng, 1, 16), rnd_safe_seg(rng, 8, 32)]
    # Include percent-encoded-looking but slash-free literals to interact with unescape logic in other paths
    # Even though literals are sanitized, these are valid because '%' is allowed and no '/'
    enc_like = ['percent%20space', 'dash-%2D', 'u%7Bvar%7D', 'star%2A']
    base += enc_like
    # Ensure none are '.' or '..'
    base = ['seg' if s in ('.', '..', '') else s for s in base]
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in base:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out

def pack_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically reads up to a null or length from corpus chunk; we provide NUL-terminated strings.
    return s.encode('utf-8') + b'\x00'

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = bytearray()

    # Provide a pool of strings consumed across multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in stubs.
    segs = themed_segments(rng)

    # Many stubs request up to ~6 strings; provide more to be safe.
    # Order them to increase chances of matching routes: pairs like (a,b) then variants.
    ordered = []
    if len(segs) >= 2:
        # pair variants for /a/b and /a/{var}
        ordered += [segs[0], segs[1]]
    ordered += segs

    # Cap total size
    for s in ordered:
        b = pack_c_string(s)
        if len(buf) + len(b) > MAX_BUF - 64:
            break
        buf += b

    # Append several unsigned ints for branching choices used by stubs
    # Use values to explore both branches: small pattern of bits and randoms.
    uints = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0xFFFFFFFF]
    uints += [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(8)]
    for v in uints:
        if len(buf) + 4 > MAX_BUF:
            break
        buf += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

    return bytes(buf)
